rules.citation: Part I, Title XXI, Chapter 151B, Section 4
rules.title: Unlawful housing discrimination and rental screening practices
rules.requirement: Landlords, managers, brokers, agents, condominium or cooperative organizations, and others with authority over covered housing may not refuse to rent, sell, negotiate, or provide different terms because of protected characteristics, public assistance or housing subsidy status, children, disability-related needs, or sexual harassment. They also may not make discriminatory rental inquiries, records, notices, statements, or advertisements, and covered disabled tenants may request reasonable modifications or accommodations.

coverage.small_owner_exception: The statute exempts the leasing of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling when the other unit is occupied by the owner as the owner's residence; the children/familial-status subsection also has limited exemptions for certain small elderly or infirm occupied dwellings and temporary leasing of an owner's principal residence for not more than one year.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Coverage depends on whether the property is a publicly assisted, multiple dwelling, contiguously located, or other covered housing accommodation, terms defined outside this excerpt.
coverage.summary: Applies broadly to covered Massachusetts rental housing and housing-related services, including owners, lessees, brokers, managers, agents, and condominium or cooperative organizations, subject to specific small-owner, senior-housing, and occupancy-related exceptions.

rules.exemptions: The age provisions do not apply to minors or qualifying elderly, 55-or-over, or 62-or-over housing. The law states that familial-status protections do not limit local, state, or federal maximum-occupancy restrictions and exempts certain small dwellings occupied by an elderly or infirm person, temporary leasing or subleasing of an owner's principal residence for up to one year, and a single unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling. The section also preserves certain preferences by religious or denominational institutions or related charitable or educational organizations.
rules.interaction: The statute says familial-status protections do not limit local, state, or federal maximum-occupancy restrictions, and it provides that, notwithstanding any contrary general or special law, by-law, or ordinance, rent or other charges for handicap-accessible housing may not be higher than for comparable nonaccessible housing.
